correctness.rationale: For each boundary alignment, wholly observed blocks must avoid u and the two partial end blocks can always be extended to allowed blocks using the free symbol and |Σ|≥2. This includes the case of a word contained in one partial block. Thus a missing factor has an occurrence in every residue. Selecting one per residue gives a spanning path with gaps either proper periods or at least k+1; Kruskal's component numbers are the successive gcds, yielding the lower bound. Conversely, join translated copies of a subgroup path by positive steps p_i. Its endpoint shift within the smaller subgroup has no effect on the sequence of quotient cosets, and the last k+1-step stage generates the remaining quotient. Each stage yields exactly the recorded difference in copy-count-weighted component numbers. For any nonconsecutive overlapping copies the intervening gaps are all periods, and the sum below k is a period by chaining the defining symbol equalities. Hence all prescribed occurrences can coexist and attain the bound. The empty list and period-one cases, strict drop for a bordered word, and length-25 example check. Independent subset BFS on an explicit per-codeword path automaton confirmed all 241 binary holes at k=2–6 and ternary holes at k=2–4 combined; source scripts were inspected, not run. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py 3; output /workspace/branches/independent_replay.out.
residual_risks: The finite BFS tests corroborate the argument; extension to every alphabet and block length is analytical.

evidence: Chandelkar–Chadha give a general upper bound 4k²−3k and an exact unbordered example a^{k−1}b. Gusev–Pribavkina give the exact length for a different family deleting multiple words of two lengths. Boccuto–Carpi discuss bounds in unambiguous automata.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A uniform upper bound cannot identify individual distances by proper periods; the special example is again unbordered. A multi-hole, nonuniform family does not specialize to this exact arbitrary single-hole family.

evidence: The earlier closed form lacks any of the proper-period weights. The general newer result is a bound and the exact example has no proper period.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Agreement for the unbordered case or use of the same residue criterion does not imply a lower bound sharp for simultaneous overlapping periods. The subgroup-coset path realization matching the spanning-tree cost supplies the extra argument.

evidence: Pribavkina Prop. 2 proves k²+k−1 for the one-hole uniform code with an unbordered deleted block. Fici–Pribavkina–Sakarovitch Prop. 2.3 states this result and cites [2], Pribavkina. Some sources say incompletable rather than uncompletable.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Absence of borders is exactly the empty period list. Their proven number agrees on this domain; neither proposition takes multi-period words as inputs. The finite concatenation factor definition and the one-hole code conditions do agree on the shared subdomain.
searches: Resultary title and semantic queries: one-hole uniform codes; uncompletable words and period–gcd formula

evidence: Catalogue search found no equivalent census; 746f0dfb3273 concerns minimal absent factors of evolving periodic prefixes. Pribavkina's unbordered theorem gives an exact subdomain, not a table of bordered instances.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Minimal absent factors of one prefix are not missing factors of arbitrary allowed codeword concatenations. Even a bounded table of examples would not cover the stipulated unbounded block lengths and alphabets; no all-length tabulation or theorem was found.
searches: Resultary: exact title and one-hole/uncompletable-word period–gcd formulations

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the exact formula for all one-hole fixed-length codes, in particular the interaction of multiple proper periods. The unbordered answer was already known, and the reduction to alignment obstructions is not itself novel. The frozen wording suggesting an independent second presentation is imprecise: Fici–Pribavkina–Sakarovitch explicitly attribute their proposition to Pribavkina (2009). No examined source covers the general bordered formula.
residual_risks: Unindexed and equivalent graph/automata formulations may exist.
Full text of the finite deciphering delay paper was not accessible; no verdict on that source individually.

value.rationale: This resolves the naturally parameterized shortest obstruction problem beyond the benchmark unbordered case. It gives a cheap computation from periods without materializing the allowed code and explains how successive periods affect attainable length. The matching constructive path proves the arithmetic is not just a lower bound or fit to small cases.
residual_risks: The result does not classify all shortest obstructions or solve the analogous multi-hole problem.
